Show HN: Comemo – composite memory provider for Hermes Agent
items.summary: There are many memory providers that can be used externally with Hermes Agent. However, like many other AI agents, Hermes only provides one slot for an external memory provider. Comemo takes that slot and acts as a composite provider. How? It fans out memory writes to multiple backends such as Mem0, Honcho, and Supermemory. On retrieval, it queries the enabled providers, merges their results, and removes duplicates before returning them to Hermes. I intend to add support for more memory providers and eventually extend Comemo to other open-source AI agents with similar limitations.

items.title: Show HN: Tyrus – TypeScript Syntax. Rust Semantics. Programming Language
items.summary: Four months ago, I got curious about building my own programming language. All I wanted was for it to be written in Rust and compiled to native code. My initial goal was simply to print "Hello World" in the terminal. I pulled it off, and from there, I kept adding more features. I knew absolutely nothing about compilers when I started. Along the way, I discovered a whole new world of concepts: parsing, semantic analysis, AST, ASan, LSan, UB, LLVM, IR, drop glue, double free, LSP, and so on. Today, I feel like I know maybe 5% of it. Now it's time to fix all the bugs that will inevitably show up.

items.title: Show HN: ExtensionSafe – see what a browser extension's code actually does
items.summary: I built ExtensionSafe after not being able to find a reliable way to figure out if a browser extension is safe to install. The other crx checkers and extension scanners mostly just check permissions and for eval() calls in the code, but fail to actually find malicious behavior. I built extensionsafe around LLMs that gives an evidence-based abuse and risk profile based on the extensions actual functionality from the code.
